articles.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection as it looks to ‘begin the next chapter’
articles.summary: Saudi investors stopped backing LIV this year. Rahm and DeChambeau still involved. LIV Golf, the breakaway tour that spent billions luring top players away from the PGA Tour, has filed for bankruptcy protection in the United States, it announced on Tuesday.
body: Launched in 2022, free-spending LIV caused shockwaves and bitter divisions in the golf world, before losing the backing of its deep-pocketed Saudi investors this year, prompting a scramble to stay afloat.

“This process gives us the structure and time to pursue a landmark transaction and begin the next chapter of LIV Golf,” said the chief executive, Scott O’Neil, whose organisation had already laid off the majority of its staff this month.

O’Neil said LIV still intends to return in a new form next year “built around the fans, an innovative, player-first ownership model, and a part of the global golf ecosystem.” But “no definitive decisions regarding the 2027 schedule or individual events are being announced at this time,” the statement added.

Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF) had spent an estimated $5bn on the tour before abruptly pulling the plug this year. LIV Golf is also seeking recognition of the US bankruptcy filing in England and Wales to cover its international assets and operations.

articles.title: Real Madrid cling on to beat Inter on Mourinho’s big Champions League night
articles.summary: Sometimes football is silly and sometimes it is more fun for it. On a night when there were 37 shots and the goalkeepers shared thirteen saves between them, some of them absurd, José Mourinho’s Real Madrid found a way to beat his former team Inter in his first Champions League night of his second…
body: You would say that they had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried, Courtois would probably save that too. This wasn’t always good, in fact at times it was terrible, but they had got through somehow. When Madrid scored the first, this grand arena cheered but they might as well have laughed too. That Madrid led really didn’t make much sense; not when it came to the goal and not when it came to the game either. It had taken Madrid four minutes to get a meaningful hold of the ball, and by then Courtois had already made a superb save from Marcus Thuram. But now, somehow, they led. Ninety minutes later, they still did.

Inter had been playing round them with what looked like an ease, until suddenly even the simplest things looked complicated. Hakan Calhanoglu had just fired off the third shot and Lautaro Martínez the fourth when it happened. Inter had enjoyed 65% of possession which actually felt like rather more until then suddenly gave it up, and in a way that was comic.

articles.title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music, then oversaw a gritty performance that ended with Manchester City enjoying the sweet notes of victory.
body: They had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition and also lost the 2021 Champions League final at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.
Factor in, too, how City face Paris Saint-Germain on matchday No 2, and travel to Manchester United for Sunday’s derby, and Maresca can be exuberant at his start as Pep Guardiola’s successor.

All four games have been won – maybe more than even he would have hoped for, Erling Haaland’s double keeping the perfect start going. With 16 points the accepted target to qualify automatically for the knockout stage, as this was required in the first two years of this format, Maresca may have considered a win here vital particularly as targeting four victories from City’s four home matches as necessary to reach the tally might founder due to the visit of the double European champions next month.

Maresca stood down Elliot Anderson and gave Ayyoub Bouaddi a full debut, alongside Enzo Fernández in midfield. Haaland was not given the rest Maresca stated he will need at some point soon, as the No 9 headed an attack that contained Phil Foden, Rayan Cherki and Antoine Semenyo behind.

articles.title: Cullen leads late Pears rally against Northants
articles.summary: Henry Cullen and Jake Libby hit half-centuries as Worcestershire recover from a mid-innings slump in their County Championship game against Northants.
body: Northamptonshire skipper Luke Procter took 5-63 to help his promotion-chasing side bowl out Worcestershire for 200, but not before the hosts were bolstered by a late-order maiden half-century from Henry Cullen.
The young wicketkeeper made 64 following Jake Libby's earlier half-century (55), while Adam Hose (45) was the only other man in double figures.
Supported by Harry Conway (2-38), Procter led from the front as the Pears middle order slumped from 103-2 to 150-9, before Cullen's late counter-offensive.
Northants openers Ricardo Vasconcelos and Procter, who was struck a painful blow amidships, then negotiated a tricky eight-over spell late in the day to close on 16-0.

articles.title: Morgan stars as Middlesex bowl out battling Durham
articles.summary: Ben Raine leads a Durham fightback with the bat after Seb Morgan's four wickets had put Middlesex in the driving seat on day one at Chester-le-Street.
body: Ben Raine led a Durham fightback with the bat after Seb Morgan's four wickets had put Middlesex in the driving seat on the opening day of their County Championship fixture.
An even morning session burst into life in the final over, with Morgan taking two wickets from three balls to put promotion-chasing Durham in a spot of bother at 80-4.

Morgan got the key wicket of Durham skipper Alex Lees just after lunch and a rain delay halted Middlesex's progress for a brief period. Ryan Higgins then picked up the baton upon resumption with three wickets.
However, Durham fought back through a final wicket stand of 90 between Raine (58*) and Callum Parkinson (26) before they were bowled out for 252.

articles.title: Hewett and Reid bid for sixth US Open title
articles.summary: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid start their bid for a sixth wheelchair doubles title at the US Open with a dominant victory in New York.
body: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid started their bid for a sixth wheelchair doubles title at the US Open with a dominant opening victory in New York.
Playing Frenchman Stephane Houdet and China's Zhenxu Ji, the British top seeds sealed a 6-3 6-1 win to progress to the semi-finals.
They will next face Japan's Tokito Oda and Argentina's Gustavo Fernandez, the 2025 champions at Flushing Meadows.
Hewett, 28, and Reid, 34, have 25 Grand Slam doubles titles as a pair and begin their singles campaigns on Wednesday.

articles.title: MAC Challenges Michigan Win, Big Ten Fires Back
articles.summary: The Big Ten is not backing away from the replay decision that gave Michigan one final chance against Western Michigan. Hours after the Mid-American Conference challenged the replay procedure used at the end of Michigan’s stunning 13-12 victory, the Big Ten issued a brief response Tuesday and made…
body: “The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination made by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter.”

The response comes after MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher said further review determined that the Big Ten replay crew did not follow the established protocol when deciding whether one second should be restored. The MAC’s official statement says the replay crew should have used the clock displayed on the program feed rather than the clock embedded within the Big Ten replay system.
That distinction is significant because it changes the argument surrounding Michigan’s miracle finish.

The Big Ten’s original explanation of the final second focused on synchronized replay video showing Western Michigan defensive back Micah Davis touching the football while established out of bounds with one second remaining.

articles.title: Willock grabs late goal as Newcastle edge Millwall
articles.summary: Joe Willock's late goal sent a relieved Newcastle into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup as the Premier League side scraped to a 1-0 victory at Sky Bet Championship outfit Millwall.
body: Just before going ahead, the Magpies had been given a fright when a shot from Tairyk Arconte hit a post, with the hosts at that point threatening to upset the competition's winners of two seasons ago.
The Lions brought on 15-year-old midfielder Regan Anderson, who became Millwall's second youngest player, in the time that remained, but Newcastle held firm in what was a hard-fought tie.
Jacob Murphy bent a shot harmlessly over in the early exchanges in what was the first meeting between the two teams since 1993.

The first time Millwall's debutant goalkeeper Filip Marschall was called into action was in the 15th minute when he parried Willock's strike into the air, with the ball dropping to left-back Elkan Baggott rather than the lurking Yoane Wissa.

articles.title: Haaland scores twice in win over Porto but Man City struggle to impress
articles.summary: Erling Haaland's double earned Manchester City a 2-0 win at FC Porto - but it was another game where Enzo Maresca's side won but struggled to convince.
body: City's main man up front was surprisingly wasteful in the first half, seeing two glorious chances in the area saved by Diogo Costa as well as heading another good chance over the bar.
Porto's goalkeeper was in inspired form in the opening 45 minutes, also saving well from Rayan Cherki from the rebound of one of Haaland's chances.
But Haaland took just two minutes of the second period to make amends, barging Jakub Kiwior aside to nod an Enzo Fernandez cross in off the post.

But City then took their foot off the gas as the Portuguese champions started to grow in confidence. Porto failed to produce a shot on target but Alan Varela curled just wide of the far post from the edge of the box in a warning shot.
